svg.title: Azure Local private path
svg.desc: This diagram focuses on traffic originating at the Arc resource bridge appliance VM. The Azure Local host remains beside the appliance as the provider of Arc proxy and the existing gateway tunnel, not as an independent traffic source. Packet motion is continuous and illustrative; reduced-motion preferences hide moving packets. Non-bypassed Arc resource bridge HTTPS uses the cluster IP proxy, which forwards to the host Arc proxy. Supported destinations use the existing host Arc gateway HTTP CONNECT tunnel through the enterprise firewall, ExpressRoute or site-to-site VPN, and Azure Firewall explicit proxy. The appliance does not create a separate tunnel or gateway. Other required public HTTPS uses the explicit-proxy path. The solid teal bypass originates at Arc resource bridge and connects to internal endpoints or private endpoint IPs without the cluster IP proxy, host Arc proxy, explicit proxy, or Arc gateway. Required bypass entries are part of the appliance proxy configuration. The dotted gold HTTP path also originates at Arc resource bridge and uses Azure Firewall explicit proxy without either Arc proxy hop or Arc gateway. The dashed teal private endpoint path is different: Arc resource bridge HTTPS first reaches the host Arc proxy through cluster IP, and Arc proxy uses direct private-network access for private destinations outside gateway coverage. One generic Private endpoints box represents the alternative private access paths. Internal endpoints stay on-premises. No host OS traffic or host-originated bypass is shown.

path.title: Non-bypassed HTTP starts at the Arc resource bridge appliance VM and uses the enterprise firewall and private connection to reach Azure Firewall explicit proxy. It does not enter the cluster IP proxy, host Arc proxy, or Arc gateway. No independent host HTTP traffic is shown.

Azure Firewall explicit proxy forwards permitted HTTP to the required public endpoints. This path branches to Azure public services or continues to third-party internet endpoints; it does not use Arc gateway or private endpoints.
The explicit proxy forwards permitted HTTP to a required Azure public endpoint. The Azure-services component groups destinations; each service determines which protocols its endpoints accept.
Arc gateway HTTP CONNECT tunnel: host Arc proxy to the public Arc gateway, carried through the enterprise firewall, ExpressRoute or site-to-site VPN, and Azure Firewall explicit proxy.
The Arc gateway forwards gateway-supported HTTPS to Microsoft-managed Azure services.

Required public-endpoint HTTPS outside Arc gateway coverage uses the enterprise firewall, private connection, and Azure Firewall explicit proxy. Its branches reach Azure public services or third-party internet endpoints, not private endpoints.
Required Azure endpoints not supported by Arc gateway are reached directly through Azure Firewall explicit proxy on the Azure backbone, not through the third-party public-internet area.

Arc resource bridge HTTPS for private endpoint FQDNs outside gateway coverage reaches Arc proxy through the cluster IP proxy. Arc proxy connects directly to the private IP using the enterprise firewall and private connection as network transit, without Azure Firewall explicit proxy or Arc gateway. This is distinct from the solid teal appliance-side bypass. DNS must resolve the private IP on the host for this forwarded path.

The Arc resource bridge appliance sends traffic for its configured bypass destinations directly to the private endpoint IP in the VNet. The enterprise firewall and private connection provide network transit. This appliance-originated route skips cluster IP proxy, host Arc proxy, Azure Firewall explicit proxy, and Arc gateway; it does not originate at the Azure Local host.

Local branch of the appliance-side bypass line before the enterprise firewall. Arc resource bridge traffic to required internal endpoints uses local network routing and does not enter either proxy or the Azure private connection.
The Arc resource bridge appliance sends outbound HTTPS to the Azure Local cluster IP proxy.
The cluster IP proxy forwards resource bridge traffic to the host Arc proxy, reusing its existing Arc gateway HTTP CONNECT tunnel.
